title: One-Sided Limits on a Piecewise Function
caption_md: This graph shows the piecewise function $f(x) = x + 1$ for $x < 2$ and $f(x) = 5$ for $x \ge 2$. Drag the epsilon slider toward 0 to squeeze in on $x = 2$ from both sides. Notice that the left-hand approach settles near $y = 3$ while the right-hand approach settles near $y = 5$. Because $\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x) = 3 \neq 5 = \lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x)$, the two-sided limit does not exist. The open circle at $(2, 3)$ reminds you that $f(2) = 5$, not 3 — the function value at $c$ is separate from the limit.
